welcome.mcp.intro: Claude can run the Swiss Knife tools for you — you just ask in plain language. Works with Claude Desktop and Claude Code.
welcome.mcp.steps:
1.  Click Connect Claude Desktop above.
2.  Quit Claude Desktop completely and open it again.
3.  Ask Claude and give it the full path of your file — for example:
welcome.mcp.examples:
•  “Check that every image used in /path/joker.json exists in joker.atlas.”
•  “What could be optimised in /path/joker.json? Don't change anything yet.”
•  “Export the first frame of animation win from /path/joker.spine as a PNG.”
Claude only changes a file when you tell it to apply the change, and a backup is saved first. Export tools need the Spine editor installed.

keyframe.info2: Detects and removes redundant animation keyframes: a key is removed only if the value interpolated between the remaining neighbouring keys stays within the tolerance for every removed key. The tolerance applies to translate (units) and rotate/shear (degrees); scale and colour channels (0..1) use tolerance x 0.01. Keys with bezier/stepped curves, and attachment, twoColor, deform, constraint and event timelines are never touched.
